title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Overboost Condition
shortDescription: DTC P0234: turbocharger/supercharger overboost condition fault detected.
fullDescription: DTC P0234 indicates Turbocharger/Supercharger Overboost Condition. This range covers turbocharger/supercharger boost control, wastegate solenoids, charge-air cooler hardware, and diesel intake air flow. Sustained underboost or overboost can damage the turbo and engine.
safetyImpact: Boost control failures cause power loss, limp mode, and on diesels excessive smoke/EGT that can crack pistons or damage the turbo.

causes.cause: Cracked or disconnected charge pipe / intercooler hose
Boost pressure sensor out of range

fixSteps.title: Scan and Pressure Test
fixSteps.instruction: Read all codes and freeze-frame. Smoke-test the charge-air system for leaks.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Turbo Hardware
fixSteps.instruction: Remove charge pipe; check for shaft play, oil, and damaged compressor wheel.

fixSteps.title: Test Boost Solenoid / Actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Command the wastegate / VGT actuator with the scan tool; measure travel.

fixSteps.title: Replace Failed Component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace solenoid, actuator, sensor, or turbo as indicated. Reset adaptations.

faq.q: Can I drive with a turbo code?
faq.a: Most cars enter limp mode and limit boost. Drive gently to a shop; sustained operation can damage the turbo.

faq.q: Is a boost leak the most common cause?
faq.a: Yes — split intercooler hoses and loose clamps cause more turbo codes than failed turbos.

faq.q: Is this a DIY repair?
faq.a: Hose and clamp work is DIY. Turbo replacement is a professional job on most modern engines.

Boost pressure sensor out of range

fixSteps.title: Scan and Pressure Test
fixSteps.instruction: Read all codes and freeze-frame. Smoke-test the charge-air system for leaks.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Turbo Hardware
fixSteps.instruction: Remove charge pipe; check for shaft play, oil, and damaged compressor wheel.

fixSteps.title: Test Boost Solenoid / Actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Command the wastegate / VGT actuator with the scan tool; measure travel.

fixSteps.title: Replace Failed Component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace solenoid, actuator, sensor, or turbo as indicated. Reset adaptations.

faq.q: Can I drive with a turbo code?
faq.a: Most cars enter limp mode and limit boost. Drive gently to a shop; sustained operation can damage the turbo.

faq.q: Is a boost leak the most common cause?
faq.a: Yes — split intercooler hoses and loose clamps cause more turbo codes than failed turbos.

faq.q: Is this a DIY repair?
faq.a: Hose and clamp work is DIY. Turbo replacement is a professional job on most modern engines.
